newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Yilmaz says to debate polls in coalition.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Yilmaz says to debate polls in coalition.

text.p: Turkey's new Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz said on Monday he would debate a date for possible early elections with his coalition allies.
"Negotiations on an election date will be carried out among the coalition partners," Yilmaz told a news conference after being appointed prime minister by President Suleyman Demirel.

Secularist Yilmaz said no date for elections was mentioned in the government protocol, despite having said earlier that any government of his would probably hold polls in early 1998. General elections are due to be held by the year 2000.
The government forged by Yilmaz out of Turkey's splintered parliament is a minority coalition of three parties that is supported by a fourth parliamentary grouping

The coalition must now face a confidence vote in parliament within around 10 days. A wave of resignations from an opposing conservative party have given him an apparent majority in the 550-member assembly.
The government is being set up to prevent a return to power by the outgoing Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan, who resigned two weeks ago under pressure from the secularist army.
